sections.title: Intake
sections.conclusion: Baseline fields and source anchors establish whether the proposal can be reviewed at all.

sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Requested: Treasury withdrawal to reimburse a lost 100,000 ADA Info governance action deposit and 3,000 ADA in claimed lost staking rewards.
Deliverables: Reimburse the lost Ikigai Info governance action deposit., Compensate the submitter for claimed lost staking rewards., Distribute the funds directly on-chain upon enactment.
Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, medium materiality): An Info governance action titled "Cardanoの生きがい - Ikigai -" was submitted in September 2024 after the Chang hard fork.

Claim (governance, supported_in_proposal, low materiality): The Ikigai Info governance action was symbolic and asked the community whether they agreed with a statement of thanks and hope for Cardano's future.

Claim (technical, proposer_asserted, high materiality): The submitter lost the 100,000 ADA deposit because a Cardano node bug permitted use of an unregistered stake key and prevented deposit recovery.
Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): There was significant community sentiment at the time that the Ikigai deposit should be reimbursed.

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The Cardano in Oceania initiative included this reimbursement in a budget Info governance action, but that governance action was not approved.
Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The requested 103,000 ADA consists of the original 100,000 ADA deposit plus 3,000 ADA for staking rewards calculated at 2% per annum.
missing: Independent evidence for: The submitter lost the 100,000 ADA deposit because a Cardano node bug permitted use of an unregistered stake key and prevented deposit recovery.
Independent evidence for: There was significant community sentiment at the time that the Ikigai deposit should be reimbursed.
Independent evidence for: The Cardano in Oceania initiative included this reimbursement in a budget Info governance action, but that governance action was not approved.
Independent evidence for: The proposal states there are no additional costs or expenses associated with the treasury withdrawal.
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Treasury analysis
findings: Six-month treasury flow regime: unsustainable (basis: total inflow (tau + donations) vs enacted withdrawals)
sections.conclusion: Treasury votes require a higher bar because they consume shared ADA and create precedent.

sections.title: Risk review
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "An Info governance action titled "Cardanoの生きがい - Ikigai -" was submitted in September 2024 after the Chang hard fork." and clears the evidence gates.

Strongest NO: a material claim is unsupported — "The submitter lost the 100,000 ADA deposit because a Cardano node bug permitted use of an unregistered stake key and prevented deposit recovery." — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit.
Strongest hold: if claims cannot be tied to replayable evidence, abstaining avoids overclaiming certainty.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
sections.conclusion: The vote is only credible if the assessment tree shows enough work for a skeptical delegator to audit.
